title: Secrets of the Heavenly Realm
next_chapter_hook: At the moment Chen Ji gazed into the abyss, from two distant corners of the mortal realm, two threads of fate pierced through the void toward him—the prayers of Su Qingyao and Ye Qing, crossing the boundaries of three realms.

text.content: Deep in the heavenly realm, stars were like grains of sand. The Tianji Record floated before Chen Ji, its characters writhing like living things, and across from him, the being called Cang Yutian observed him in a manner beyond mortal comprehension. No face, no form—only a pair of eyes composed of endless constellations, cold and eternal. "You've finally arrived, Chen Ji." The voice came not from any direction but directly within Chen Ji's consciousness. "Or should I say, Test Subject Number 7734."

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian slowly unfurled a luminous curtain, revealing a vision that made Chen Ji's pupils contract sharply—an endless void, billions of light points floating within like sands of the Ganges, and each light point imprisoned an entire world. "The Heavenly Realm, the Mortal World, the Demonic Domain—merely experimental fields created by the cosmic will for its own evolution. You think you've been scheming against the world? No, you were merely selected as a sample to filter optimal solutions. Through three thousand cycles of reincarnation, geniuses, prophets, and chess pieces like you have been helping the cosmic will find a way to break through its own limitations."

text.content: Chen Ji stared at that luminous curtain, his knuckles white from tension. Rage churned in his chest like molten lava, but habits cultivated over years forced him to suppress the impulse to erupt. Instead, a cold smile twisted his lips. Test Subject. Sample. Optimal Solution. He carved each word into his bones. All his imagined chess games, his schemes, his resistance—everything had become a joke. But Chen Ji had never lacked the courage to start over. He only became more certain of one thing—all debts owed to him would be repaid with interest. "Continue," he heard himself say, his voice unnaturally calm for someone who had just learned he was an experiment. "Since you've brought me here, finish what you have to say."

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian seemed slightly surprised by his composure. A flicker passed through those constellation eyes. "Interesting. More composed than the previous 7,333." The luminous curtain shifted, displaying a scene achingly familiar to Chen Ji—his father Chen Tianming, young and vibrant, standing before an ancient altar, his eyes burning with ambition identical to his son's. "Your father was the test subject closest to breaking through. He almost touched the core of the cosmic will, falling short by only the final step." Cang Yutian paused, and something almost resembling... regret tinged the voice. "Unfortunately, he failed. Thus, he was sealed, erased, completely removed from history. Do you think those rumors of his betrayal came from nowhere?"

text.content: Chen Ji's breath halted for a moment. Father. That figure, already blurred in his memories, that answer he had pursued for countless years—revealed in such a manner. He recalled fragments from childhood—his father holding him, saying: "Ji'er, Father is going somewhere very far. When Father returns, I'll show you the true stars." So those supposed stars were merely the edges of a cage these ants could never reach. Rage scorched his rationality like wildfire, but Chen Ji knew better—the anger at this moment was meaningless. He slowly closed his eyes, turning that fire threatening to burst from his chest into a sharp blade. The blade pointed outward, and inward. "I've noted it," he opened his eyes, his voice terrifyingly soft. "What else?"

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian gazed at him, and something seemed to calculate within those constellation eyes. "You now have two choices." A forked path appeared in the luminous curtain. "First, inherit your father's遗志, replace me as the new cosmic will, continue this experiment, and filter the next optimal solution for the universe's evolution. Second—" The luminous curtain suddenly dimmed, transforming into a void that devoured everything. "—perish with the old will. Your Tianji Record, your Heavenly Fate Value, all your karmic bonds, will become fuel for the universe's rebirth. Three thousand worlds return to nothingness, and you won't even leave behind a grain of dust."

text.content: Chen Ji stood in place, his robes flapping violently in an inexplicable wind. He looked around at those billions of imprisoned worlds, then suddenly laughed. The laughter rose from low to high, echoing through the empty heavenly depths, carrying a near-mad recklessness. "I read a book in my previous life," he stopped laughing, his voice growing colder, "that said when fate gives you two choices, it often means a third option is being hidden. Cang Yutian, or rather—" He raised his head, staring directly into those constellation eyes, speaking word by word: "—the so-called Eye of Heavenly Dao, are you certain you have the right to decide Chen Ji's fate?"

text.content: Cang Yutian fell silent for a moment, then produced a laugh difficult to interpret. "Interesting. Your father asked the same question once. Unfortunately, transcending requires a price, and your筹码—" The luminous curtain suddenly changed, displaying a scene Chen Ji never expected: his sister Chen Nian, imprisoned by countless chains in some unknown abyss, eyes tightly closed, the Heavenly Fate mark on her forehead being slowly stripped away by some force.

text.content: Cang Yutian let out a profound sigh. The constellation eyes slightly narrowed, as if examining an unqualified creation. "You're as arrogant as your father. But at least he tried to seize power. You don't even dare to try?" Deep in the heavenly realm, a sudden tremor—the imprisoned worlds began flickering madly, an apocalyptic force rushing toward Chen Ji from all directions.

text.content: At the moment Chen Ji spoke those words, the Tianji Record suddenly shuddered. Those fragmentary characters began to flicker madly, countless sealed chapters unsealed themselves, and an old yet familiar voice came from deep within the pages—"Ji'er, you've finally come." It was his father's voice. Chen Ji's eyes instantly grew moist, but he had no time for sentiment, for the Tianji Record was reshaping itself visibly, page after page of newborn knowledge flooding into his consciousness like a tide.

Cang Yutian's Star River Eye suddenly contracted, the array composed of those points of light beginning to show signs of disorder.
"Impossible—" For the first time, that eternally cold voice carried a tremor, "The seal on the Tianji Record Fragment was set by my own hands, how could that rebellious remnant soul possibly—"
"Because he never intended to truly perish." Chen Ji cut it off, the curve of his lips carrying a cold glee. He reached toward the Tianji Record, and the book actually flew willingly into his palm, pages fluttering like butterflies, revealing the ultimate chapter never seen by anyone.
"My father never believed in any so-called optimal solution, he only believed in—" Chen Ji's voice grew clearer in trembling fury, "—risking everything for a desperate chance."

The ultimate chapter of the Tianji Record slowly unfolded, Chen Tianming's old yet resolute face emerging between the lines of text. His voice crossed the boundary of life and death, echoing clearly through this realm of heaven:
"Ji'er, when you see these words, it means you've walked the path I could not complete. What Cang Yutian does not know is that the true purpose of the Tianji Record is not to foresee, but to—"
"—weave." Chen Ji chimed in, his voice overlapping with his father's, striking a thunderous echo in the void, "It is not the cosmic will that weaves fate, but we who consider ourselves mere chess pieces."

dialogue.content:
Cang Yutian finally revealed its true form—a massive eye woven from countless threads of destiny, each thread connecting to the rise and fall of a world.
"Enough!" Its voice was no longer the previous coldness, but carried an unmistakable... fear? "You ants, thinking that by relying on a broken artifact you can oppose—"
"A broken artifact?" Chen Ji coldly laughed, raising the Tianji Record high, "Then why did you use it as the standard for selecting us from the very beginning? What are you afraid of, Cang Yutian? Afraid that these ants you speak of would one day overturn the chessboard you've so carefully arranged?"

text.content:
The Tianji Record bloomed with dazzling light in Chen Ji's hands, those fragmentary characters rearranging and combining into intricate formations. His father's will poured into Chen Ji's consciousness like a warm flood, carrying a profound entrustment.
"Ji'er, your father spent his entire life searching for only one possibility—" Chen Tianming's voice gradually faded, "—to reclaim the authority of the Tianji Record from the Hand of Heavenly Way. And the key lies within the bond between you and Nian'er."
Chen Nian. That sister taken away by the Holy Sect, used as a Heavenly Fate Lock Key, was currently sleeping in some unknown abyss. And the mark on her brow was precisely the final link connecting the Tianji Record to the cosmic will.
"You were scheming against me!" Cang Yutian roared, those threads of destiny madly lunging toward Chen Ji, "You think you can succeed? Your father failed, and you will fail too!"

Chen Ji did not dodge, nor did he counterattack. He simply stood quietly in place, allowing those threads of destiny to缠绕上 his body, to wind around the Tianji Record.
Because he felt it. Among those threads, one was especially different—thin, dim, yet radiating a familiar warmth. That was his father's remnant will, the foreshadowing he had buried using his last trace of strength.
"Father," Chen Ji murmured softly, a wild smile matching his father's appearing at the corner of his mouth, "This chess game of yours, you've truly played it grand."
The Tianji Record suddenly erupted with a pillar of冲天光芒, that light piercing the clouds, breaking through the barrier of the heavenly realm, shining toward the distant lower world—toward those two figures praying for him.
At this moment, in the mortal realm.
At the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain, Su Qingyao's eyes snapped open, a flash of astonishment in her gaze. She felt a summons, the aura of the Tianji Record—it was Chen Ji!
At the same time, in a hidden corner of the demonic realm's frontier, Ye Qing also sensed something, her demonic path mist-like aura somehow resonating with that light.
Two strands of bond power, crossing three realms, converging toward Chen Ji.

In that instant, Chen Ji perceived it.
Su Qingyao's trust was like a sword, Ye Qing's reliance was like a shield, two strands of bond power piercing through the experimental field's shackles, flooding into his body, intertwining with his father's remnant will.
The Tianji Record completed its final transformation in this moment. Those threads of destiny originally controlled by Cang Yutian began to loosen, shatter, and reorganize under the impact of three forces. Chen Ji's consciousness touched an indescribable realm in that instant—he saw Cang Yutian's true form, saw the真实面貌 of those billions of light-point worlds, and also saw the path no one had ever walked.
"Impossible!" Cang Yutian's voice carried true terror now, "That is a heavenly net I spent countless eons to weave completely, how could you possibly—"
"Because we are chess pieces." Chen Ji's voice was calm yet firm, "And the greatest strength of chess pieces lies precisely in—"
He raised his head, directly facing those Star River Eyes trembling violently from fear:
"—when all chess pieces move simultaneously, the player must also dance along."

Deep within the heavenly realm, a thunderous rumble suddenly erupted. Those threads of destiny that had maintained the experimental field's operation for countless eons began snapping apart inch by inch.
Cang Yutian let out a final howl, a sound containing unwillingness, fury, and an indescribable sense of relief. But Chen Ji had no time to contemplate these things, for among the broken threads of destiny, he finally caught that thread connecting to Chen Nian—
It was still there.
And following that thread, he sensed his sister's faint yet tenacious life force, along with the Heavenly Fate mark on her brow that was beginning to awaken.
"Nian'er..." Chen Ji murmured softly, the first time he had shown such obvious emotional fluctuation before anyone. The fury gradually receded, replaced by an unprecedented resolve.
He silently made a vow in his heart—no matter the road ahead, no matter how many schemes he still had to face, he would find her. This time, he was not acting as a test subject, but as a brother.
"Next stop," his voice echoed through the gradually collapsing heavenly realm, carrying undeniable ruthlessness, "Going to find my sister."
